name: Adrenaline (epinephrine)
class: Sympathomimetic – α and β agonist; vasopressor / inotrope
status: PILOT – † lines checked against package insert 2026-11-15; awaiting review

pi_source.title: Adrenaline (Epinephrine) 1 mg/1 ml (1:1 000) Fresenius – professional information (SAHPRA repository, Oct 2022)

dagger_note: † = general pharmacology; not in the SA guideline and not stated in the package insert consulted
item_format: t=text, s=source:printed page (s=pi: package insert), d=dagger, n=from own notes, b=bold, h=heading
summary: First-line in anaphylaxis and cardiac arrest; infusion for shock not responding to fluids; nebulised for stridor.

forms.t: Injection 1:1000 = 1 mg/mL, 1 mL ampoule (contains sodium metabisulphite)
1:10 000 (0.1 mg/mL): dilute 1 mL of 1:1000 in 9 mL sodium chloride 0.9% or sterile water

moa.t: α: vasoconstriction and rise in blood pressure
β₁: cardiac stimulation; β effect on airways gives bronchodilation
Reduces mucosal oedema and stabilises mast cells in anaphylaxis

pk.t: Effects are short-lived because of rapid inactivation in the body
IV onset immediate; IM onset about 5 minutes; inactive orally; metabolised by COMT and MAO

items.t: 0.5 mL of 1:1000 IM immediately into the anterolateral thigh; repeat every 5 minutes as required
Persistent hypotension or multiple repeat doses: IV infusion, start 0.05 mcg/kg/minute, titrate to response
0.01 mL/kg of 1:1000 (undiluted) IM (= 10 mcg/kg); max 0.5 mL per dose; repeat every 5 minutes if necessary
IV infusion 0.02 mcg/kg/minute: mix 0.06 mg/kg in 50 mL dextrose 5%; 1 mL/hour = 0.02 mcg/kg/minute
1 mL of 1:1000 (1 mg) IV or IO immediately; flush with 5–10 mL sterile water or sodium chloride 0.9%; repeat every 3–5 minutes
0.1 mL/kg of 1:10 000 IV/IO (= 10 mcg/kg); follow each dose with a small bolus of sodium chloride 0.9%
Shockable rhythm: repeat after every 2nd shock, i.e. every 4 minutes
ETT adrenaline is no longer recommended
IV infusion, start 0.05 mcg/kg/minute (post-cardiac arrest: 0.1 mcg/kg/minute), titrate to response
Range 0.01–1.0 mcg/kg/minute; aim for MAP > 65 mmHg within 30 minutes
Nebulise 1 mL of 1:1000 diluted in 1 mL sodium chloride 0.9%, with oxygen, every 15–30 minutes until expiratory obstruction is abolished

administration.t: Adult infusion: 10 mg (10 ampoules of 1:1000) in 1 L sodium chloride 0.9% = 10 mcg/mL
Rate at 0.05 mcg/kg/minute: 50 kg = 15 mL/h; 60 kg = 18; 70 kg = 21; 80 kg = 24; 90 kg = 27; 100 kg = 30 mL/h. Multiply for higher doses (0.1 mcg/kg/minute = double)
IM into the anterolateral thigh; avoid the buttock (risk of tissue necrosis)
Extravasation may cause tissue necrosis and sloughing
Give infusions through a large vein where possible

adjustments.t: Crosses the placenta; use only if the benefit justifies the risk. Parenteral use is not recommended during the second stage of labour (may delay it and cause uterine atony)
Distributed into breast milk; avoid breastfeeding during treatment

contraindications.t: Contraindications are relative, because adrenaline is used in life-threatening emergencies
Do not inject into fingers, toes, ears, nose or genitalia (ischaemic necrosis)
Monoamine oxidase inhibitors, or within 14 days of stopping them

cautions.t: Heart disease, cerebrovascular disease, hyperthyroidism, diabetes, phaeochromocytoma, narrow-angle glaucoma, severe renal impairment, the elderly
Non-selective β-blockers: severe hypertension and reflex bradycardia; anaphylaxis may respond poorly
Tricyclic antidepressants potentiate the effect; halogenated anaesthetics may induce ventricular fibrillation
Check the concentration (1:1000 vs 1:10 000) before every IV dose

adverse_effects.t: Palpitations, tachycardia, hypertension, potentially fatal ventricular arrhythmias, myocardial ischaemia / infarction

monitoring.t: Observe for 24 hours after anaphylaxis for a biphasic reaction
Continuous ECG, BP and pulse during IV use

toxicity.t: Overdose: symptomatic and supportive; a rapidly acting α-blocker (phentolamine) followed by a β-blocker has been used

conflicts.t: Package insert: the 1:1000 solution is not suitable for IV use and must be diluted to 1:10 000 before IV use. The Adult STG gives 1 mL of 1:1000 IV followed by a flush in cardiac arrest. The pathway follows the STG.
